summary: Surveyed the unit's full file list: every file carries the .lean extension, matching the corpus-wide check that across all 19 mathlib4 review units (7659 files) 100% are .lean. Ran a whole-word grep for theorem|lemma|def|structure|class|instance|inductive|abbrev|example|axiom across the whole Mathlib tree to find files with no declaration keyword at all (182 of ~7840 tracked .lean files). Read every such file that falls in this unit completely. 122 of the 182 corpus-wide are `deprecated_module (since := ...)` redirect stubs produced by Mathlib's file-reorganization tooling (e.g. Mathlib/Data/Complex/Basic.lean, Mathlib/Data/Real/Sqrt.lean): a one-line module header, one import of the file's new location, and the deprecated_module command. These are themselves the navigation/redirect content a reader needs to find where a declaration moved, so excluding them would remove the only pointer rather than duplicate one. The remaining 60 are tactic/notation/attribute-registration modules such as Mathlib/Tactic/ToAdditive.lean (attribute assignments), Mathlib/Data/Int/Notation.lean (a notation declaration), and Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Elementwise.lean (an attribute application) -- FILTER-007 explicitly places `open`, notation, attributes, options, aliases, and namespace commands outside the pure-import-only class, so these carry formal interface content and stay in the primary index. No file in this unit is a generated artifact, test fixture, vendored copy, script, or non-Lean file.
